 # ===========================================================================
 # 20 — Console I/O: portable `puts` / `print`
 # ===========================================================================
 # Character: a side effect with no portable VALUE — but a portable SHAPE. `puts`/`print`
 # are auto-injected front doors (ADR-0068/0069/0083, `Rian.IOStdlib`) over the per-target
-# host output — `IO.puts` (BEAM) · `console.log` (JS) · `println` (Kotlin). No import, no
-# boilerplate: a program that calls them gets their bodies emitted into it.
+# host output — `IO.puts` (BEAM) · `console.log` (JS) · `println!` (Rust) · `println`
+# (Kotlin). No import, no boilerplate: a program that calls them gets their bodies emitted
+# into it.
 #
 # They take a `String | Int53` value union (ADR-0083), so a number prints with no explicit
 # conversion — the `Int53` arm stringifies via `Prim.int_to_string` (portable). `print` is
 # the same without the trailing newline.
 #
-# REACH `[:ex, :js, :jvm]`, NOT `:rs` (the `#@reach` header above is the honest matrix): the
-# value-union arm hands the host's `&str` parameter an owned `String`, and the Rust
-# owned→borrow coercion across a value-union arm is a tracked follow-up — so `:rs` is
-# honestly OFF rather than a false claim.
+# Reaches **all four targets**. The value-union arm hands the host's `&str` parameter an
+# owned `String` member; the Rust emitter borrows it across the arm (`&s` / `&n.to_string()`,
+# the `owned_binders`/`owned_arg?` borrow), so the `println!`/`print!` bodies type-check.

 #
 # RETURN TYPE `Unit` (ADR-0068): a console call has no meaningful value, and its

-# needs an owned→borrow coercion across the value-union arm the emitter does not yet do

+# Reaches **all four targets**. The polymorphic `puts` is a value-union (ADR-0083) that hands
+# `line` an owned `String` member; the Rust emitter borrows it across the value-union arm
+# (`&s` / `&n.to_string()` — the `owned_binders`/`owned_arg?` coercion), so the `println!`/
+# `print!` host bodies type-check.
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
 # a line to stdout, with a trailing newline (the raw per-target host call). Named `line`,
 # not `puts`, so it does not clash with the bare polymorphic `puts` front door.
 @external(:ex, "IO.puts(s)")
 @external(:js, "console.log(s)")
+@external(:rs, "println!(\"{}\", s)")
 @external(:jvm, "println(s)")
 pub def line(s val String) Unit
 
 # raw text to stdout, no trailing newline. (`:js` targets node.)
 @external(:ex, "IO.write(s)")
 @external(:js, "process.stdout.write(s)")
+@external(:rs, "print!(\"{}\", s)")
 @external(:jvm, "print(s)")
 pub def write(s val String) Unit
